title: Set detection of the Ext orthogonal of exact flat-cycle complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ be the class of unbounded cochain complexes in $\mathcal A$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] which are acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and have flat cycle sheaves $Z^nP=\ker(d^n:P^n\to P^{n+1})$ for all integers $n$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. There is a set $S_{\mathrm{ex}}\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ such that
$$\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\perp_1}=S_{\mathrm{ex}}^{\perp_1}$$
in the abelian category of complexes. Explicitly, for every complex $T$, every short exact sequence $0\to T\to E\to P\to0$ splits for every $P\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ if and only if this holds for every $P\in S_{\mathrm{ex}}$. Smallness of the site suffices; no enough-points, boundedness or sectionwise-flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated set-detection foundation for proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction. WANTED: Recktenwald (2019), Proposition 2.5.37, https://d-nb.info/1211326829/34 (read online, not archived): the small ringed-site argument, not just the ringed-space case. No Stacks tag supplies this set-cogeneration assertion.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)$. The smallness hypothesis gives the Grothendieck property of $\mathcal A$ by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]; then [lem-coef-complexes-grothendieck] gives it for $\mathcal B$. We will use exact filtered colimits in both categories. Colimits of complexes are computed degreewise: take the colimit of each term, induce the differentials from their compatible cocones, and verify $d^2=0$ on each cocone map; the same universal property makes this the colimit complex. Write $|P|=|\coprod_{n,U}P^n(U)|$.

source.place: Infrastructure for paragraph 2; Grothendieck sheaf category: Stacks Tags 03DA/03DB; degreewise construction of colimits of complexes.

proof.text: Flat sheaves are closed under filtered colimits. Indeed, the tensor-Hom adjunction of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and the colimit universal property give, for every $N,H$, $\operatorname{Hom}(N\otimes\varinjlim F_i,H)\cong\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(N\otimes F_i,H)$, naturally in $H$, so $N\otimes\varinjlim F_i\cong\varinjlim_i(N\otimes F_i)$. Tensoring a short exact sequence with each flat $F_i$ is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; exactness of filtered colimits in Step 1 makes the colimit tensor sequence exact. Applying the same exact-colimit argument to $0\to Z^nP_i\to P_i^n\to P_i^{n+1}$ shows $Z^n(\varinjlim P_i)=\varinjlim Z^nP_i$, and exactness of $\varinjlim P_i$ follows by taking colimits of the exact rows $0\to Z^nP_i\to P_i^n\to Z^{n+1}P_i\to0$. Consequently $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ is closed under small filtered colimits. No claim that sheaf colimits are sectionwise is made.

source.place: Elementary adjunction/colimit calculation: Stacks Tags 03EP (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-commute-colimits) and 03EU (sites-modules-lemma-colimits-flat).

proof.text: For a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to U\to V\to W\to0$ with $U$ acyclic, the cycle sequence $0\to Z^nU\to Z^nV\to Z^nW\to0$ is short exact. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], forgetting the module action preserves kernels and cokernels (these have the same sectionwise kernel and sheafified sectionwise cokernel); it therefore preserves and reflects epimorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] to the underlying abelian sheaves. To see surjectivity of the cycle map, locally lift a section $w\in Z^nW$ to $v\in V^n$. Its differential lies in $Z^{n+1}U$, hence, after a further covering, is $d_Uu$ for $u\in U^n$ because $U$ is exact. Then $v-u$ is a cycle lifting $w$. The kernel is $Z^nU$ directly. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], if two of $U,V,W$ are acyclic then the third is acyclic. Flat sheaves are closed under extensions by [lem-coef-module-flat-cotorsion-foundation]. Thus extensions of two objects of $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ are in that class. Also if $U,V$ are in it and $Z^nV/Z^nU$ is flat for every $n$, then $W$ is in it and $Z^nW\cong Z^nV/Z^nU$.

source.place: Elementary cycle lifting plus the cited long exact sequence and flat extension closure; compare Recktenwald Proposition 2.5.37, final paragraph, online.

source.place: Recktenwald Proposition 2.5.37, initial nonzero cycle; fixed cardinal enlargement for all following rows, online.

proof.text: Construct $N^j\subseteq P^j$ and $L_j\subseteq Z^jP$ successively for $j=n-1,n-2,\ldots$. Given $L_{j+1}$, apply [lem-coef-small-flat-subextension] to the exact row $0\to Z^jP\to P^j\xrightarrow{d^j}Z^{j+1}P\to0$ and its flat subsheaf $L_{j+1}$. Its hypotheses hold: $P$ is exact, $Z^jP$ is flat, $L_{j+1}$ is flat of size at most $\kappa$, and the cardinal equation was checked in Step 4. The lemma supplies $N^j\subseteq(d^j)^{-1}(L_{j+1})$, of size at most $\kappa$, mapping epimorphically onto $L_{j+1}$, with $L_j=N^j\cap Z^jP$ and both $L_j,Z^jP/L_j$ flat. The inclusion $L_j\subseteq N^j$ also shows $|L_j|\leq\kappa$, so the next application has the required bound. The differential is the restriction of $d_P$ followed by $L_{j+1}\hookrightarrow N^{j+1}$. These formulas give $d^2=0$ and the exact rows $0\to L_j\to N^j\to L_{j+1}\to0$. This is ordinary recursion on $n-j\in\mathbf N$, not a choice of a lowest degree.

source.place: Recktenwald Proposition 2.5.37, downward construction of equations (10) and (11), online; the new lemma packages only one finite row.

proof.text: The rows just constructed show $Z^jN=L_j$ for $j\leq n$ and $Z^jN=0$ for $j>n$, and that $N$ is acyclic. Thus $N\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ and $N\ne0$ since $N^n=L_n\ne0$. It has $|N|\leq\aleph_0\kappa=\kappa$. Every quotient $Z^jP/Z^jN$ is flat (for $j>n$ this is $Z^jP$). Step 3 applied to $0\to N\to P\to P/N\to0$ therefore gives $P/N\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}$. We have proved, by an explicit construction, that every nonzero object of this class has a nonzero subcomplex of size at most $\kappa$ in the class, with quotient still in the class.

source.place: Verification of the preceding construction, corresponding to Recktenwald Proposition 2.5.37 after equation (11), online.

proof.text: There is a set of isomorphism classes of complexes with $|N|\leq\kappa$: in each degree and at each site object replace the section set by a subset of a fixed set of cardinality $\kappa$, and encode addition, scalar multiplication, restrictions, and differentials by functions between these sets. The indices $\mathbf Z$, the objects, the arrows, and the sections of $R$ are sets, so the collection of all such structures is a set. Restrict to those satisfying the sheaf, complex, acyclicity and flat-cycle conditions and choose one representative of each isomorphism class. Call this set $S_{\mathrm{ex}}$; its members are in $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$.

source.place: Set of bounded structures; compare the set displayed in Recktenwald Proposition 2.5.37, online.

proof.text: Every $P\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ admits a small continuous filtration $0=P_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq P_\lambda=P$ with successive factors isomorphic to members of $S_{\mathrm{ex}}$. Maintain $P_\alpha,P/P_\alpha\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}$. At a successor with $P/P_\alpha\ne0$, use Step 6 on that quotient, and take the inverse image of the resulting small subcomplex as $P_{\alpha+1}$. Then $P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$ is that subcomplex and $P/P_{\alpha+1}$ its quotient; Step 3 gives the asserted membership of $P_{\alpha+1}$. At a nonzero limit $\beta$, set $P_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}P_\alpha$. Exactness of filtered colimits embeds this colimit into $P$ and identifies $P/P_\beta$ with $\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}(P/P_\alpha)$. Step 2 proves both are in the class. The process terminates: subcomplexes of $P$ form a set, since each is a family of subsets of the fixed section sets $P^n(U)$; strict successors cannot be chosen for an ordinal larger than the cardinal of this set. Choose such an ordinal in the fixed universe and stop at the first zero quotient. All colimits used therefore have small ordinal indices. If $P=0$, take $\lambda=0$.

source.place: Explicit filtration argument underlying Recktenwald Lemma 2.5.24; filtered-colimit closure from Steps 1-2; no appeal to its unexposed proof.

proof.text: Let $T\in S_{\mathrm{ex}}^{\perp_1}$ and let $0\to T\to E\xrightarrow{p}P\to0$ be short exact in $\mathcal B$, with $P\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}$. Use the filtration of Step 8 to construct compatible maps $s_\alpha:P_\alpha\to E$ with $p s_\alpha$ the inclusion into $P$. Start with the zero map. Given $s_\alpha$, apply the lifting clause of [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus] in the abelian category $\mathcal B$ to $i:P_\alpha\hookrightarrow P_{\alpha+1}$, $p:E\twoheadrightarrow P$, $a=s_\alpha$ and $b:P_{\alpha+1}\hookrightarrow P$. Its hypothesis holds because $\operatorname{Coker}(i)=P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$ is isomorphic to an element of $S_{\mathrm{ex}}$ and $\operatorname{Ker}(p)=T$. The filler is $s_{\alpha+1}$, and it agrees with $s_\alpha$ exactly, so the induction maintains compatibility. At a limit, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] supplies the unique map from $P_\beta$ induced by the compatible $s_\alpha$; composition with $p$ is the inclusion because it agrees on every cocone map. At $\lambda$ this gives $p s_\lambda=1_P$. Thus every such extension splits and $T\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\perp_1}$.

source.place: Explicit compatible-splitting proof of the set-detection implication (Recktenwald Lemma 2.5.24, online); lifting statement cited in precisely its mono/epi form.

proof.text: Since $S_{\mathrm{ex}}\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal F}$, an object orthogonal to every member of $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ is orthogonal to every member of $S_{\mathrm{ex}}$. Combined with Step 9 this proves the asserted equality and its short-exact-sequence interpretation. Every use of an epimorphism in the construction was sheaf-local; no points, boundedness of the original $P$, or sectionwise flatness was assumed.
